initial_claims.claim_text: The PandaRoot event generator supporting single particles whose parameters advance in fixed patterns is FixStepParticleGun, implemented by the class PndFixStepParticleGun.

Stepping in momentum is configured using SetPRange(pmin, pmax, pstep), while stepping in polar angle is configured using SetThetaRange(thetamin, thetamax, thetastep) or SetCosThetaRange(costhetamin, costhetamax, costhetastep).

In the generator execution sequence, the particle gun is first instantiated and configured with its step ranges, initialized through Init(), and then invoked event-by-event via ReadEvent(FairPrimaryGenerator *primGen) during the simulation run.

initial_claims.claim_text: PandaRoot's operational documentation establishes an ordered multi-stage workflow: event simulation via sim_complete.C, detector response simulation and local reconstruction via digi_complete.C, tracking via reco_complete.C, track-PID combination via pid_complete.C, and final analysis via ana_complete.C.

Across the execution chain, simulation produces the intermediate simulation file (such as simFile / sim.root), which is consumed by FairRunAna during digitization in digi.C to generate the intermediate digitized output (digiFile); this digiFile is then consumed downstream by FairRunAna in reco.C to produce the reconstructed file (recoFile).

PandaRoot includes the helper class PndFileNameCreator, which initializes from the simulation file path and defines methods including GetDigiFileName() and GetParFileName() to derive digitization and parameter file names, but the supplied evidence does not establish whether it provides methods or extensions for reco and pid files.
The workflow evidence identifies curated_panda_domain as part of the requested data flow.

PandaRoot Macros
¶
Macros Folder
¶
The folder /macros contains the steering macros for PandaRoot. They are usually called via
root macroname.C
and the file name is identical to the macro name.
Most important folders are:
[master](./master/mastermacros.md):
Contains the standard macros to perform a complete simulation chain
tools:
Collection of useful macros for e.g. the event display or additional MC track information
Description of folders:
data:
Empty folder were by default the generated data of the macros is stored to
detectors:
Sub-detector specific macros
examples:
Various example macros
outdated:
Macros not used anymore
params:
Parameter files serving as an input to detector simulations
production:
Scripts and macros for larger simulation campaigns
QA:
QA macros used to test the proper running of PandaRoot
run:
Macros to run complete simulation chain with full control over the used tasks
softrig:
Macros used for the software trigger
timebased:
Macros to run time-based simulations
tracking:
Macros to run the different tracking and trackingQA algorithms
tutorials:
Tutorial macros used at various PandaRoot workshops
@ingroup group_macros
# Master Macros
These ROOT macros run a complete chain of a default PandRoot simulation. They employ the so-called Master run and Master Tasks, which are tools to provide default settings and operation modes.
It is not important where you store the macros. You may copy the whole folder to a place of your liking.
Keep in mid to source the
config.sh -p
script to set up each terminal you are using.
## First Steps
If you simply want to simulate & reconstruct some events with default settings you’ll need only 2 commands:
Starting with a simulation (here 100 events)
`
root
-l
-b
-q
sim_complete.C'(100)'
`
you may process the detector answer and reconstruction in one go:
`
root
-l
-b
-q
full_complete.C
`
and subsequently run an analysis
`
root
-l
-b
-q
full_complete.C
`
Modify the macros to suit your purpose. The sections below introduce the options.
## Output Stages
Instead of running everything in one go
`
root
-l
-b
-q
full_complete.C
`
you may run each stage separately. It is particularly useful if you want to have extra root files for each stage or if you want to stop processing at a certain stage.
`
root
-l
-b
-q
digi_complete.C
root
-l
-b
-q
reco_complete.C
root
-l
-b
-q
pid_complete.C
`
`
root
-l
-b
-q
ana_complete.C
`

Master Macros
¶
Introduction
¶
The master macros are the standard simulation and reconstruction macros of PandaRoot.
They use the
MasterTasks
to have the most recent default settings for the detector simulation.
Running
¶
The typical sequence of macros is:
sim_complete.C - Event simulation. Set here the event generator you want to use
full_complete.C - Digitization, tracking and PID in one go
ana_complete.C - Analysis of the data. Adopt here your analysis method
A sequence which expands the digi, reco and pid ito separate steps is:
sim_complete.C - Event simulation. Set here the event generator you want to use
digi_complete.C - Detector response simulation and local reconstruction
reco_complete.C - Tracking
pid_complete.C - Combine tracks with PID information
ana_complete.C - Analysis of the data. Adopt here your analysis method
Common User Settings
¶
It is encouraged that you copy the macros to a location of your choice and work from there.
For your own analysis you have to modify the
sim_complete.C
macro to set the proper event generation. EvtGen mostly serves for signal events, FTF for continuum background, while the BoxGenerator is there for detector studies.
Also you have to write your own analysis.

initial_claims.claim_text: Besides the Dual Parton Model (DPM), the E760 model (E760 parameterization) was studied as the alternative hadronic elastic-scattering model for PANDA luminosity determination, where the theoretical elastic differential cross section serves as the reference distribution compared against the measured LMD angular distribution to extract the absolute luminosity as a normalization parameter.

The E760 parameterization is implemented directly as code in the LuminosityFit software alongside the DPM parameterization, although DPM was chosen for thesis studies to match PANDA's official event generator.

The thesis reports that the intrinsic model uncertainty of the E760-like model is approximately 2% at a beam momentum of 1.5 GeV/c, decreases to 0.1% between 3 and 6 GeV/c (staying below 0.5% across the 2 to 8 GeV/c range where it was originally tuned), and rises slowly back to 2% at 15 GeV/c.

Regarding beam momentum, the thesis notes that beam momentum is fixed and measured with a relative precision of a few hundred keV/c, allowing it to be treated as a constant, while the supplied evidence does not document a separate added beam-momentum uncertainty contribution evaluated for the E760 model.

answer_points.text: How PandaRoot's fast simulation produces detector responses instead
Which building blocks PandaRoot's fast simulation is made of

initial_claims.claim_text: Instead of executing full Geant particle transport through matter and detector digitization/reconstruction, PandaRoot's fast simulation produces detector responses by taking initial generator particles and either removing them according to detector acceptance or smearing their properties based on the statistical characteristics of fully simulated events.
The simulation framework executes via FairRunSim with Geant tracking disabled (primGen->DoTracking(kFALSE)) and runs the PndFastSim task to generate the simplified detector responses.

PndFastSim is assembled from detector components registered via AddDetector—spanning electromagnetic calorimeters (EmcBarrel, EmcFwCap, EmcBwCap, EmcFS), tracking and vertexing detectors (Mvd, Stt, MdcTS, MdcFS), and particle identification detectors (DrcBarrel, DrcDisc, Rich, Tof)—and can optionally integrate a neutral hadronic split-off parametrization module configured through EnableSplitoffs.

answer_points.text: How PndRecoKalmanTask turns input PndTrack objects into fitted output tracks
How fitter selection is handled in PndRecoKalmanTask
How particle-hypothesis choice is determined in PndRecoKalmanTask
How each persisted result is constructed in PndRecoKalmanTask

initial_claims.claim_text: In PndRecoKalmanTask, input PndTrack objects are received from the input TClonesArray fTrackArray (configured via SetTrackInBranchName), fitted via the GenFit framework using the selected fitter, optionally propagated toward the interaction point or across a specified distance, and saved as fitted tracks into fFitTrackArray.

In PndRecoKalmanTask, the constructor instantiates both PndRecoKalmanFit (fFitter) and PndRecoDafFit (fDafFitter); fitter selection and execution mode are configured through member flags such as fDaf (toggled by SetDaf, defaulting to kFALSE) to select Deterministic Annealing versus standard Kalman fitting, along with fUseGeane (SetGeane) and fTrackRep (SetTrackRep).

Particle hypothesis selection in PndRecoKalmanTask is governed by fPDGHyp, which defaults to 211 (pion) and can be set explicitly through SetParticleHypo, or configured to obtain the Monte Carlo truth hypothesis from fMCTrackArray when fIdealHyp is activated via SetIdealHyp.

Persisted fit results in PndRecoKalmanTask are stored in fFitTrackArray, a TClonesArray initialized for PndTrack; each persisted PndTrack object encapsulates the first and last fitted track parameters (FairTrackParP), the associated PndTrackCand, fit quality metrics including chi2 (fChi2) and NDF (fNDF), a quality flag (fFlag), and the PID hypothesis (fPidHypo).

initial_claims.claim_text: In the restgas reconstruction sequence configured in macro/target/reco_complete.C and documented in README.md, PndUnassignedHitsTask executes after the standard reconstruction by PndTrkTracking2 to collect the detector hits (including STT, MVD, and GEM) left unassigned by the standard track finder.

Downstream of hit collection, the displaced-track finder stage PndApolloniusTripletTrackFinderTask reconstructs displaced two-dimensional track trajectories in the xy-plane using STT drift-circle triplets combined with MVD and GEM hits, outputting intermediate ApolloniusTripletTrack and ApolloniusTripletTrackCand data products.

Following the 2D triplet reconstruction and prior to the final Kalman fit, the z-recovery stage PndSttSkewStrawPzFinderTask consumes ApolloniusTripletTrack and ApolloniusTripletTrackCand along with skewed STT hits to calculate wire intersections and recover the longitudinal coordinate (z) and momentum component (pz), handing off the reconstructed FinalTrack and FinalTrackCand products to PndRecoKalmanTask2.
The workflow evidence identifies curated_panda_domain as part of the requested data flow.

initial_claims.claim_text: Within the PandaRoot framework, LMD detector digitization and hit reconstruction are handled for the HVMAPS sensors by the SDS package, followed in sequential order by Track Finding, Track Fitting, and Track Filtering and Back-Propagation.

In the LuminosityFit repository, simulation and reconstruction workflows are orchestrated via python scripts such as doSimulationReconstruction.py (or doReconstruction.py) and runSimulationReconstruction.py, which manage configuration files like sim_params.config and reco_params.config.

Following simulation and reconstruction, LuminosityFit orchestrates the interaction-point evaluation, correction dataset generation, and subsequent luminosity fit via determineLuminosity.py, with the underlying fit executable invoked through runLmdFit.sh.

initial_claims.claim_text: In the initial vertex-finding pass, following track reconstruction and PID without back-propagation in pid_complete.C, ana_dpm.C calculates the proton-antiproton POCA and exports two intermediate outputs for the second analysis pass: the file <prefix>_boost.root containing an event_poca tree (storing event_id, x, y, z, and a valid flag), and <prefix>_vtx_fit.json containing the fitted sample-level vertex means and widths.

To feed the vertex results into the reprocessing stage, the orchestration routine in poca_step2_analysis.py parses the fitted mean vertex coordinates from the JSON file into the environment variables FIT_VERTEX_X, FIT_VERTEX_Y, and FIT_VERTEX_Z, and passes the path to <prefix>_boost.root via the POCA_VERTEX_FILE environment variable.

During the second pass reprocessing in prod_aod_complete.C under the 'fitvertex' configuration, PndPidCorrelator consumes the event_poca tree from POCA_VERTEX_FILE to propagate each event's tracks to its per-event POCA, while using the FIT_VERTEX_* environment variables as a fallback target, prior to final NTuple creation in ana_complete.C.

What the two propagators behind the GEANE and analytic helix options are

initial_claims.claim_text: The two propagators behind the GEANE and analytic helix options in PandaRoot are PndGeanePro and PndHelixPropagator, both derived from PndPropagator.

PndGeanePro determines the transported track state by invoking GEANE (calling ERTRAK via the GEANT3 interface), which numerically integrates the equation of motion using Runge-Kutta extrapolation through the magnetic field map.

PndHelixPropagator determines the transported track state analytically assuming a circle projection in the xy plane and straight or helical motion along the magnetic field, calculating the position and momentum at a target z-position, arc length, angle, or point of closest approach.
